title: tying a fact to the work that produced it: server-side provenance for row one
excerpt: Row one of the ARTEX audit ended with an open question: the label deciding whether a fact can prove a goal was written by the model the target is talking to. I posted the rule for fixing it and then implemented it, so a fact now has to quote a line of the intent's recorded activity before it counts as evidence, and bytes the proxy captured coming back from the target are stored as target_response whatever the model declared.

title: agentlens: score a coding model on its first attempt, not its final one
excerpt: A harness that snapshots the workspace at every done claim, so a model's first attempt gets scored before it has a chance to correct itself.

title: auditing an agent's memory: enforced provenance, self-declared labels
excerpt: ARTEX's maintainer invited an adversarial audit of the platform's own agents, and the memory poisoning row holds up better than expected: fact provenance is enforced down to a prove_goal refusal, but the label deciding which gate applies is written by the model the target is talking to.

title: the truncation guard stops at chat: proving the blind spot with a real vault
excerpt: A review of DeepTutor's truncation guard found the same cut-off tool calls reaching five dispatch sites outside the chat path, so I filed the issue with a runtime repro: a scripted truncated round, the real dispatch code, and a real Obsidian vault that gets mutated while history records a fabricated success.

title: A modern approach to securing kubernetes cluster
excerpt: This is an update of Rob Thorne's 2021 Medium article, *Adventures in Encryption: Securing Your Laptop Kubernetes Cluster*, with credit to Rob for the original approach. Part I covers a local cluster, and Part II takes the same ideas to a public cluster with free Let's Encrypt certificates.

title: triage without a reproduce step: what's left for an outside contributor

title: from a compose file to a certificate chain

title: where the deeplink work can make money, and the reporting trap that kills it
excerpt: Desk research on which programs pay for nonce-laundering XSS: Basecamp/HEY on HackerOne ($100-$10,000, with a 2026 cross-account nonce-bypass chain already disclosed) is the closest fit; Intigriti only has Lightspark and Adobe paying publicly. The trap: "CSP headers" is out of scope, but "XSS despite CSP" is not.

title: Server-side trace of the deeplink gadget: positive and negative findings
excerpt: The deeplink gadget in Mercado Libre's home component D interpolates server-rendered deeplink and redirectUrl values into single-quoted JavaScript inside a nonce'd script. Verified against the saved bundle: a mobile User-Agent flips openInApp.shouldRedirect and mounts it anonymously. But a quote nulls redirectUrl, non-UUID d2id nulls deeplink, and </script> is edge-blocked. Sink confirmed, sanitiser confirmed, no execution.

title: Dead end with test accounts and researching a workaround
excerpt: The ATO 2FA challenge test account (userId 1252539217, CHALLENGE_ATO_USER_2, site MCO) returns 302 /login/identification/not-found, suggesting it is expired or removed. Later work showed the deeplink gadget mounts anonymously for mobile UA (and is sanitised), so the account blocker now applies to the seller / second-order path. Workaround paths: seller accounts, personal account (one only, no mass creation), or waiting for program test-user rollout.
